deepdive.thesis: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited is India's second-largest public sector oil refiner and marketer, operating an extensive retail network to supply transportation fuels, lubricants, and emerging clean energy solutions while driving the nation's energy transition toward net zero by 2040.

open.item: HPCL is slated to become a Net Zero company for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2040, with energy efficiency as a major lever.
Lube Modernization & Bottom Upgradation Project at Mumbai Refinery to increase LOBS production from the current 475 KTPA to 764 KTPA.
The same Mumbai Refinery Lube Modernization & Bottom Upgradation Project will increase bitumen production by approximately 487 KTPA.

Progressive commissioning of the 9 MMTPA integrated grassroot Refinery-cum-Petrochemical project at Balotra, Rajasthan (HRRL) is in progress, with crude taken in CDU/VDU enabling sequential commissioning of secondary units.
Once fully operational, HRRL will be one of India's most advanced integrated refinery and petrochemical complexes and will significantly strengthen HPCL's downstream portfolio.

As the Residue Upgradation Facility at Visakh Refinery advances through stabilisation towards its designed operating performance, it will transform 93% of bottom-of-the-barrel residue and improve product value realisation.
Management flagged heightened geopolitical uncertainty and crude market turbulence, including the March 2026 closure of the Strait of Hormuz, as the operating terrain the Corporation must manage.
The 201 km Haldia-Panagarh LPG Pipeline is nearing completion to serve LPG demand in West Bengal, Bihar and Jharkhand.
The 540 km Visakh-Raipur Pipeline is progressing across Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
HRRL's 2.4 MMTPA petrochemical capacity is coming on stream, with HPCL building supply-chain and channel-partner readiness for the upcoming petrochemical volumes under the HP Durapol polymer brand.

risks.note: Dated Brent opened FY 2025-26 at US$ 67.7 per barrel and averaged US$ 70.3, but a March 2026 military escalation in West Asia sent prices briefly toward US$ 130 per barrel with Dubai touching US$ 169; the Board notes these geopolitical developments 'are bound to have a pronounced impact on the Corporation, in the near future.'
risks.risk: Crude oil price volatility and geopolitical supply shock

risks.note: The Strait handles approximately 20% of global oil trade and is the critical transit point for the high-sulphur grades that dominate the Indian crude basket; its effective closure in March 2026 produced a supply shock that pushed the Indian basket to a monthly average of US$ 113.5 per barrel.

Singapore complex refining margins swung from US$ 3.8 per barrel in Q2 FY 2025-26 to US$ 8.78 per barrel in Q4; annual profitability depended heavily on a back-loaded spike in middle distillate cracks rather than a broad-based margin environment.

The annual strength was driven by the substantial widening of middle distillate cracks in Q3 and Q4, with Gasoil margins climbing to US$ 24.5 per barrel in Q3; 'the sharp spike in Gasoil margins toward the end of the year, triggered by supply shock concerns, ensured that overall refinery profitability remained robust', leaving earnings exposed if the diesel crack normalises.
risks.risk: Concentration of margin in middle distillates

risks.note: Naphtha margins were the weakest segment through the year, at US$ -4.6 per barrel in Q1 and US$ -6.8 per barrel in Q2 on a sluggish petrochemical complex and a shift toward alternative feedstocks, while High Sulphur Fuel Oil 180 CST margins corrected to US$ -5.5 per barrel in Q2 and US$ -7.0 per barrel in Q3.
risks.risk: Structurally weak naphtha and fuel oil cracks

risks.note: U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports and forecasts of a significant global oil surplus in early 2026 dampened demand expectations and pressured prices through Q3, and rising non-OPEC+ output from the United States and Brazil capped prices for most of the year.
risks.risk: Demand headwinds from trade policy and a projected global oil surplus

risks.note: Maintaining throughput through the March 2026 disruption required robust crude planning and agile supply chain management; the Corporation mitigates this by processing new opportunity crudes - 10 new grades processed for the first time, taking the basket to 188 grades across nine sourcing regions including Russia.
risks.risk: Crude sourcing and supply-chain execution risk

risks.note: The Corporation is dependent on modernization and expansion of its refineries to meet growing domestic demand; the LC-Max Residue Upgradation Facility at Visakh and the Mumbai Lube Modernization & Bottom Upgradation Project must deliver designed conversion and yield to realise the intended value uplift.
risks.risk: Large-project execution and ramp risk in refinery upgradation
